findings.reason: The protected Python solution implements a 2D vector iterator (Vector2D) by tracking the current row and column indices. An internal _advance helper advances through empty or exhausted rows on demand, enabling amortized O(1) time per next/hasNext operation and O(1) auxiliary space without pre-flattening. The solution is optimal; no candidate is required.

On-demand row/column advancement in _advance guarantees that the iterator only advances past empty or completed rows when accessing or querying elements, ensuring correct sequential traversal across arbitrarily nested empty/non-empty sub-lists.

Each row is skipped at most once and each element is visited once, giving amortized O(1) time per next/hasNext call and O(N) total time over N elements. Auxiliary space is O(1) for row and column pointers. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Vector2D class initializes with vec (List[List[int]]) and provides next() -> int and hasNext() -> bool as specified in the problem contract.

The approach accurately details 2D coordinate-based lazy iteration, on-demand row-advance normalization, and amortized O(1) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover pre-flattening memory costs, empty-row skipping, and completely empty vector handling.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical 2D index-based lazy vector iterator with SHA-256 digests ffc9f44ef7a6afb5a0752105967c2fb15225e10d3cdf5ffd2176eee12d365693 and fa1dd1af8d433a289dc56e1d5f88b4c6be3c62efaec47e17466c8e255fb05038. Verified submission remains untouched.
